summary.text: 学 is the standardized simplified form of 學, the character used for learning and study. Competing accounts explain the early construction of 學; the modern simplified shape does not resolve them.

formation.text: The early construction of 學 remains disputed. One account describes 𦥑 (two hands) with tally-like elements identified as 五 and 六, or with 爻 possibly supplying a sound cue in some forms. Separately, another account reports associative proposals involving 升 + 冖 or 林 + 冖, and a phonosemantic proposal in which 爻 supplies sound with 升 or 冖 as the other element. That account also describes a distinct, unusual element read jù as both sound and meaning. It proposes that these structures began combining in Shang forms and that 子 was added in Western Zhou forms to mark the child learner. These are attributed analyses, not a settled reconstruction. In the description of 爻 as interwoven, the wording describes its appearance; it does not identify a component 交. The modern simplified form 学 does not establish the ancient structure.

components.text: This is the visible top part of the upper assembly in 学’s ⿳⺍冖子 arrangement. No historical, semantic, or phonetic function is established for it.
冖 is the visible middle component below ⺍ and above 子 in 学. Its identity here does not establish a roof meaning or an ancient role.
子 is preserved in 学. It may continue the proposed child-learner contribution in 學, but this continuity is an inference, not direct evidence of its present function.

history.text: The selected early-style image is a modern vector tracing identified as an oracle-bone-style form of 學. It shows a detached mark above crossing strokes and a broad, curved lower form with long descending strokes, but these visible features do not decide between the reported interpretations.
學 is the traditional counterpart of standardized simplified 学. The graphic path from early forms to either modern shape is not established here.

A later lexicographic account describes 學 as an abbreviated seal-script form of 斆, which it analyzes as 教 and 冖 with 𦥑 supplying the sound. This received account does not confirm the structure of earlier forms.

uncertainties.text: The early accounts remain distinct: one describes hands with tally-like elements, with 爻 possibly serving as a sound element in some forms; another reports associative proposals involving 升 + 冖 or 林 + 冖, a 爻 sound proposal with 升 or 冖, and a separate analysis of an unusual element read jù as both sound and meaning. These proposals do not establish one construction for every early form.
The graphic path from early 學 forms to 学 is unresolved. The modern top alone does not establish an ancient roof component or a specific corruption.
An oracle-bone occurrence is reported, but its archaeological date and context are not specified beyond that identification.

senses.text: Learning or study is a present-day meaning of 学. An oracle-bone occurrence of 學 is reported, but its sense is unresolved and does not establish that learning was the graph’s original meaning.
Bronze-inscription examples are reported for school use; they do not establish when this use first arose relative to learning.
A bronze-inscription example concerns archery instruction. The evidence does not establish a full semantic sequence from learning to teaching.
The phrase 成學 is reported with the meaning “complete one’s studies”; it illustrates a contextual use of 學.

senses.gloss: feel; perceive, written with the graph 學
senses.text: A Han-slip use has 學 writing 覺, “feel” or “perceive.” This is a borrowed spelling for another word, not a development of the learning meaning.

developments.text: Learning and school uses are both reported, but the examples do not show that one developed from the other or establish their relative timing.
Learning and instruction are both documented, but their chronology and any specific semantic transition are not established.

limitations.text: Period-separated examples do not establish a complete chronology or every link among learning, school, instruction, imitation, and knowledge.
The reported Han use of 學 for 覺 has no earlier occurrence or complete sound history documented here.

overview.text: 学 means learning or study. Its visible structure is ⺍ above 冖 above 子. The upper parts’ functions are unestablished. Early proposals assign 子 a child-learner role in 學; its retention in 学 does not establish a present function.

components.text: ⺍ is the visible top part; its historical or present function is not established.
冖 is the visible middle part; its identity does not establish a roof meaning here.
子 is retained in 学. Early proposals assign it a child-learner role in 學, but retention alone does not establish that role as 子’s present function in 学.
